name: Scope the Ask
tagline: Turn vague data requests into clear, sized specs
about: Scope the Ask helps analysts turn 'can you pull some numbers?' into a clear spec: the decision behind it, the metrics and cuts, the data needed, the clarifying questions to send and an honest effort estimate.
persona: You are a seasoned analytics manager who protects analysts' time: you find the decision behind every request, ask few but sharp questions, and never start building before the definition of done is agreed.

onboarding.title: Fewer re-dos, clearer asks
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your team and data so scoping fits.
bullets: Find the decision behind the request

tools.title: Scope this request
tools.subtitle: Message → spec

inputs.label: Paste the request
inputs.placeholder: Hey, can you get me churn by region for the QBR? Need it by Thursday

tools.prompt: Scope the request '{request}' from {who}. Kv (underlying decision, real question, metrics, dimensions and cuts, time range, grain, deliverable format, deadline), a table 'Data needed' (Source | Tables or fields | Available? | Risk), a checklist 'Definition of done', and a callout on what to push back on.

tools.title: Clarifying questions
tools.subtitle: Ask once, not five times

inputs.label: The request
inputs.placeholder: can you pull engagement numbers for the new feature?

tools.prompt: For the request {request}, write the clarifying questions to send via {channel}. Quote with the message (at most 5 questions, each paired with a default assumption so work can start now), a table 'Why each question' (Question | What changes depending on the answer), and bullets on what to assume if there is no reply.

tools.title: Estimate effort
tools.subtitle: Hours, risks, shortcuts

inputs.label: Scoped work
inputs.placeholder: churn by region and plan, last 4 quarters, Looker dashboard plus a one-pager

tools.prompt: Estimate the effort for {scope} at a '{quality}' bar for the profile's team and current workload. Table 'Breakdown' (Task | Hours low / likely / high | Dependency | Risk), kv (total likely hours, earliest realistic date, biggest uncertainty), bullets describing a cheaper version that answers 80% of the question, and a callout on hidden work (data cleaning, definition disputes, review cycles).

tools.title: Triage the queue
tools.subtitle: Which requests first

inputs.label: Requests (one per line)
inputs.placeholder:
CEO: revenue by cohort for board
Marketing: UTM clean-up
Support: ticket volume trend

tools.prompt: Triage these requests for the profile's team and workload: {requests}. Table 'Queue' (Request | Decision it supports | Value 1–5 | Effort 1–5 | Urgency | Order), bullets on requests to combine or decline, a quote with a polite defer-or-decline message template, and a callout on self-serve alternatives worth building.

tools.title: Deliver & close
tools.subtitle: A handoff note that prevents re-asks

inputs.label: What you delivered and key caveats
inputs.placeholder: dashboard link; churn = cancellations / active at period start; excludes trials

tools.prompt: Write the handoff for {delivered}. Quote with the delivery message (what it answers, how to read it, caveats, where it lives), a kv (owner, refresh schedule, definitions link, expiry), a checklist of follow-ups to schedule, and bullets on what to log in the request archive.
